selection_rule: Terminal/UI/architecture/code beats only. ~25 candidates extracted across the lesson's visual beats and culled to these 11; every survivor was visually inspected this session at full resolution (not just extracted). No talking-head frames. The lesson is one continuous screen recording of a custom dark-theme multi-agent observability web app (MULTI-AGENT ORCHESTRATION, 127.0.0.1:5175), so every frame is UI/code-dense; open captions (burned-in subtitles) sit on the bottom ~8% of each frame and can be cropped by the chapter builder.

frames.label: three-pillars-empty-shell
frames.shows: The empty O-Agent web app on first boot (AGENTS 0 Total, Active/Running/Logs 0, Cost $0.00, right panel 'Start a conversation — Ask the orchestrator to create, manage, or command agents', Context 0/200k) with Dan's three designed title-card overlays fading in over it: AGENT ORCHESTRATION, AGENT OBSERVABILITY, AGENTS AT SCALE.
frames.why_for_weak_student: Names the whole lesson's scaffold in one image — the three pillars (orchestrator + observability + agents-at-scale) — printed directly on the tool's starting state, so a weak learner sees both the concept and the empty canvas the rest of the demo fills. This is the mental model everything else hangs from.
frames.note: Mid-dissolve, so the browser B-roll shows faintly behind the UI; the three pillar labels and the empty-shell chrome are sharp. A cleaner fully-opaque shell exists a few seconds later without the labels; keep this one because it is the only frame that shows all three pillars named.

frames.label: command-k-capability-palette
frames.shows: The Command-K (Cmd+K) prompt palette open ('Type your command or message…') with the full capability footer: Working Directory (…/multi-agent-orchestration/apps/orchestrator_3_stream), Slash Commands (/all_tools /build /build_in_parallel /find_and_summarize /load_ai_docs /load_bundle /orch_one_shot_agent /orch_plan_w_scouts_build_review /orch_scout_and_build /parallel_subagents /plan /plan_w_scouters /prime /prime_3 /prime_cc /question /quick-plan /t_metaprompt_workflow), Agent Templates (meta-agent, docs-scraper, scout-report-suggest-fast, review-agent, playwright-validator, scout-report-suggest, build-agent), and Orchestrator Tools (create_agent, list_agents, command_agent, check_agent_status, delete_agent, interrupt_agent, read_system_logs, report_cost).
frames.why_for_weak_student: The single most information-dense frame in the lesson: it documents the ENTIRE capability surface of the orchestrator on one screen — the 8 management tools (the 'CRUD'), the seven reusable agent templates, and the ecosystem slash commands. A struggling reader can read every tool signature (e.g. create_agent(name, system_prompt?, model?, subagent_template?)) instead of trusting narration. Cross-verified against agent_manager.py.
frames.note: HERO reference frame. Text is sharp and fully readable at native resolution.

frames.label: populated-observability-3-agents
frames.shows: The differentiated multi-agent observability DX with three agents executing from a single prompt: left rail = per-agent cards (qa-agent SONNET-4.5 $0.009 ctx 352/200k; fast-frontend-qa-agent HAIKU-4.5 $0.001; fast-backend-qa-agent HAIKU-4.5) with tool/hook/response/thinking counters; center = filter tabs (RESPONSE / TOOL / THINKING / HOOK, THINKING highlighted) over a live per-agent log stream with file_path params; right = the ORCHESTRATOR message 'Perfect! I've successfully created three QA agents and dispatched tasks to all of them' with a per-agent task/output/focus breakdown.
frames.why_for_weak_student: This is the 'aha' image — 'with a single prompt, I've deployed three times the compute an engineer in a terminal has.' It makes the abstract claim concrete: two fast Haiku agents + one primary Sonnet agent, each with its own model/cost/context window, all commanded by the orchestrator, all filterable. Shows WHY observability is a pillar (you can see everything).
frames.note: On-screen model badges read SONNET-4.5 / HAIKU-4.5 — this codebase uses the newer 4.5 model family (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 / claude-haiku-4-5-20251001), NOT the sonnet-4/haiku-3.5 of the AH-3 lesson.

frames.label: the-core-four
frames.shows: Dan's 'The Core Four' designed overlay — a CONTEXT / MODEL / PROMPT / TOOLS four-circle Venn — composited over the observability UI, with the left rail still showing each agent's live core-four state (context-window bars, model badges, costs).
frames.why_for_weak_student: Ties the fleet back to the one primitive that never changes. The narration is 'we're managing the core four of every single agent we spin up… if you do not adopt your agent's perspective, you do not know what you can do.' Seeing the Venn AND the per-agent context/model/cost in the same frame makes 'manage the core four at scale' literal, not slogan.
frames.note: Same designed treatment as the tac-1 Core-Four frame; can be paired with or reinforced by a clean redrawn Venn in the chapter.

frames.label: architecture-mermaid
frames.shows: The agent-produced architecture diagram (Preview full-stack-architecture-summary.md, rendered Mermaid on a light background): Axios HTTP Client → REST API; Backend Layer (FastAPI + Python) → FastAPI Endpoints main.py → Orchestrator Service (Claude SDK Client); AI Layer (Claude SDK) → Orchestrator Agent (Claude Sonnet 4.5) → Management Tools MCP Server → Agent Manager (8 Management Tools); WebSocket /ws. Tokens: 4865.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The clearest, highest-contrast frame in the lesson and the one that answers 'how does this actually work?' A weak learner can trace the whole system: browser (HTTP + WebSocket) → FastAPI → Orchestrator Service → the Orchestrator Agent (Sonnet 4.5) → its 8-tool in-memory MCP server → the managed agents. It also proves the meta-point: the system documented itself ('using the system to build the system').
frames.note: HERO architecture frame. 'Agent Manager 8 Management Tools' == the 8 orchestrator tools in the palette frame; 'Management Tools MCP Server' == create_sdk_mcp_server(name='mgmt').

frames.label: produced-consumed-assets
frames.shows: The results-oriented view: three now-idle agents with cumulative cost/context (SONNET-4.5 $0.157 ctx 23k; HAIKU-4.5 $0.127; HAIKU-4.5 $0.173), a produced-files panel with green diff stats and Show Diff buttons (app_docs/backend-structure-summary.md +781 Added ✓Created; app_docs/BACKEND_DOCUMENTATION_INDEX.md +484 Added ✓Created) and read files (backend/modules/hooks.py 556 Read, backend/modules/subagent_loader.py 228 Read), plus an Export File Activity button.
frames.why_for_weak_student: Demonstrates 'every agent must produce a concrete result' and the Consumed-vs-Produced ledger with inline diffs — the payoff of the PITER out-loop 'Review' pillar. A weak learner sees that observing agents outside the loop still gives you diffs, costs, and one-click file access — the whole point of staying out of the loop without losing control.
frames.note: The read files are real backend source (hooks.py, subagent_loader.py), useful evidence for the codebase_map.

frames.label: crud-delete-all-agents
frames.shows: The 'D' in CRUD: right panel shows three ORCHESTRATOR ACTION cards each Tool: delete_agent with {"agent_name": "fast-backend-qa-agent"}, {"agent_name": "fast-frontend-qa-agent"}, {"agent_name": "qa-agent"}, followed by ORCHESTRATOR '✅ All agents deleted successfully! … The orchestrator is now clear and ready for new tasks.' Center consumed-files list reveals real source (backend/modules/orchestrator_service.py, database.py, config.py; frontend/src/stores/orchestratorStore.ts, services/api.ts, chatService.ts, main.ts, App.vue).
frames.why_for_weak_student: Makes the lesson's most counter-intuitive tactic tangible: 'treat your agents as deletable temporary resources… the best code is no code at all — you learn to delete.' Three delete_agent calls, work done, agents gone. Pairs with 'one agent, one prompt, one purpose' — the agent did its job and went home.
frames.note: Doubles as codebase evidence: the Pinia store is orchestratorStore.ts; the HTTP services are api.ts + chatService.ts; the orchestrator backend is orchestrator_service.py.

frames.label: ecosystem-interop-slash-commands
frames.shows: Ecosystem interoperability: the orchestrator has spun up a codebase-questioner agent (HAIKU-4.5, $0.011) and commanded it to run the /question slash command; right panel 'Agent created and task dispatched! I've created codebase-questioner (using fast Haiku model) and commanded it to run /question…'; center RESPONSE 'Answer: Yes, Both Your Orchestrator and Agents Can Use Skills. Skills are fully integrated…'; a /prime command is mid-type in the Command-K quick overlay.
frames.why_for_weak_student: Proves the claim 'interoperable with the entire Claude Code ecosystem.' The orchestrator didn't just run tools — it made a managed agent run a reusable /question prompt, and the answer confirms skills work too. A weak learner sees that everything they already know (slash commands, skills, primes) plugs straight into the fleet.
frames.note: Two ecosystem features in one frame: a managed agent running /question, and /prime being typed.

frames.label: sleep-check-agent-status
frames.shows: The orchestrator-as-glue 'sleep-check' loop with a scout+build team: left rail = build-header-pills (Template: build-agent, SONNET-4.5) and scout-header-pills (Template: scout-report-suggest-fast, HAIKU-4.5, 6k/200k, $0.032); center = '✅ Scout Report Complete… SCOUT REPORT SUMMARY, File Location: apps/orchestrator_3_…' with Consumed (frontend/src/styles/global.css, frontend/src/composables/useHeaderBar.ts, frontend/src/components/AppHeader.vue) and Produced (app_docs/header-pills-scout-report.md +363 ✓Created); right = ORCHESTRATOR THINKING 'Let me check the status again.' + ORCHESTRATOR ACTION Tool: check_agent_status {agent_name: 'scout-header-pills', tail_count: 20, offset: 0, verbose_logs: false}.
frames.why_for_weak_student: Shows two hard ideas at once: (1) agents built from templates (scout-report-suggest-fast on Haiku for read-only scouting, build-agent on Sonnet for writing) and (2) the 'sleep-check' monitoring pattern — the orchestrator polling check_agent_status while an agent works. Crucial nuance for the chapter: that ~15s poll is PROMPT-driven (Bash sleep 15 + check_agent_status in the workflow command), not hidden Python.
frames.note: Best single image of template-based agent creation (both cards show 'Template: …') + the check_agent_status tool with its exact params.

frames.label: plan-build-review-workflow
frames.shows: The three-phase ADW (/orch_plan_w_scouts_build_review) with all three agents created up front: planner-responsive-ui (SONNET-4.5, ctx 21k/200k, circled), builder-responsive-ui (Template: build-agent, 'Ready for tasks'), reviewer-responsive-ui (Template: review-agent). Center = the planner's output '…created a comprehensive 33-page implementation plan… What I Did: 1. Explored the codebase ✓' with Consumed (6 files: frontend/src/components/OrchestratorChat.vue, AgentList.vue, styles/global.css, App.vue, EventStream.vue, AppHeader.vue) and Produced (specs/responsive-ui-plan.md +1430 ✓Created 'Created responsive UI implementation plan… targeting viewports under 650px'); right = ORCHESTRATOR THINKING + ORCHESTRATOR ACTION Tool: Grep.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The lesson's climax made legible: a plan→build→review AI Developer Workflow running as three specialized primary agents, glued by the orchestrator. A weak learner can watch the planner consume real Vue components and produce a spec file, exactly the ADW shape from Tactical Agentic Coding — now spun up 'out of nowhere' by the O-agent.
frames.note: HERO workflow frame. Note the planner has NO template badge (it is created dynamically with a custom system prompt); the builder/reviewer carry Template: build-agent / review-agent. Consumed files confirm the real frontend component set.

frames.label: reviewer-verify-finale
frames.shows: The Review phase closing the loop: reviewer-responsive-ui (Template: review-agent, EXECUTING) running 'npx vite build 2>&1 | head -100' and THINKING 'Perfect! The Vite build succeeded… 1. No CSS syntax errors 2. The Vue component syntax is valid 3. The responsive styles compile correctly'; builder-responsive-ui idle ('Responsive design implemented for AgentList and OrchestratorChat on mobile viewports'). Right panel = ORCHESTRATOR THINKING 'The reviewer seems to be stuck on the same activity. Let me wait a bit longer and check again' + ORCHESTRATOR ACTION Tool: Bash {command: 'sleep 20'} then check_agent_status {agent_name: 'reviewer-responsive-ui', tail_count: 30}.
frames.why_for_weak_student: Shows the reviewer agent actually verifying the build (closing the loop) AND the orchestrator's sleep-then-check glue explicitly — 'sleep 20' + check_agent_status. This is the concrete answer to 'if something went wrong I could dial in and understand why, when, where, and who.' Verification + observability in one frame.
frames.note: Clearest single image of the sleep-check pattern as raw Bash(sleep) + check_agent_status; reinforces that the loop is prompt-driven behavior.
